summary: Well-executed, autonomy-locked paired study testing a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) guard on gpt-5-mini for 200 synthetic NetOps intents. Execution and artifact capture are comprehensive; baseline success was near-ceiling (199/200) and guarded arm reached 200/200. The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥15 pp improvement) is not supported. Main weaknesses are manuscript presentation (metadata-heavy, provenance inventory style) and a need for clearer, compact statistical and methods exposition (notably the shared-initial-generation design and exact test interpretation).
critical_issues: Manuscript presentation is metadata-heavy: large provenance and artifact inventory text appears embedded in the narrative rather than summarized in concise scholarly prose. This violates the conference guidance to use literature-grounded exposition rather than artifact bookkeeping.

Statistical reporting needs clarification: the exact McNemar two-sided p-value (reported as 1.0) and its interpretation given only a single discordant pair (n10=1, n01=0) must be explained transparently (test used, two-sided exact calculation, and implications of near-zero discordant counts).

Methods clarity around the shared-initial-generation protocol is insufficiently compact: the paper must explicitly and succinctly state (in Methods and Abstract) that baseline and guarded arms used the identical LLM-generated candidate (shared single-generation) and explain how this choice changes the estimand interpretation (measures repair efficacy on identical candidates, not performance of independent pipelines).
required_revisions: Rewrite and condense manuscript narrative to remove embedded artifact-inventory prose. Move detailed provenance, full hash manifests, and per-file listings to a single referenced reproducibility appendix or to the archived evidence bundle; replace inline listings with concise descriptions and pointers to the archived manifest (artifacts and their paths are already present).

Add an explicit, short Methods subsection (or boxed paragraph) that clearly and compactly explains the shared-initial-generation protocol: how many model calls per pair, which outputs were shared vs condition-specific, why that choice was preregistered (cost budget), and how it affects the causal estimand and external generalizability.

Clarify statistical reporting: describe the exact McNemar test implementation (two-sided exact/binomial formulation), justify its use given observed discordant counts, report the exact test input (n10, n01), state how the p-value was computed, and add an explicit sentence interpreting p=1.0 in the context of a single discordant pair and the near-ceiling baseline. Retain the bootstrap CI but add a brief note linking its utility under low-discordance scenarios.

Replace any remaining template- or provenance-style paragraphs in the main five pages with standard scholarly prose (concise background, methods, results, interpretation). Preserve all disclosure content but compress it to meet the five-page constraint while keeping the mandatory details (models, prompt reference, autonomy lock, preregistration, repair budget, seeds, and validator).

Include in the Method/Results a one-paragraph discussion of the practical consequence of the shared-initial design for operational realism and a pointer to any exploratory (independent-generation) analyses in the evidence bundle if present; if no such artifacts exist, explicitly state that independent-generation comparisons are future work.
optional_revisions: Include a compact evidence-to-claim table (one small table) mapping principal claims to the archived artifact paths/hashes (this can be short and placed near the end or in a single-column box).

Provide one short representative example (<=1 short paragraph) in the main text showing an initial faulty candidate, the repair prompt/trace, and the post-repair validator result (use the archived exemplar traces), to help readers grasp the repair effect without browsing the bundle.

Add a sentence quantifying the practical cost/latency tradeoff of the shared-generation + single-repair budget (provider-call counts are recorded; a short numeric statement would aid operational readers).
